items.title: 1 Thing I Wish I'd Known About the Stock Market When I First Started Investing
items.summary: What is the most expensive habit a new investor can pick up? Taking quick profits on a company worth owning for decades.

items.title: Should Qualcomm Stockholders Worry About Its Shrinking Revenue?
items.summary: Qualcomm (QCOM) grew revenue just 1.9% over the last twelve months, against a compound pace of about 6.2% a year over five years and 4.5% over three. The quarterly path is worse. Across the last four quarters, year-over-year growth slid from 10.0% to 5.0%, then to declines of 3.5% and 4.0%. That turn to shrinking quarterly sales is the risk to weigh.

items.title: Wall Street Just Erased $57 Billion From Micron. The Shortage Behind Its Boom Is Getting Worse.
items.summary: Micron just posted the highest revenue guidance in its history while the shortage fueling its growth gets worse, yet Wall Street wiped out tens of billions in market cap anyway. The signal hiding inside that contradiction is worth understanding before the next move.

items.title: Micron’s Powerful Economics 101 Lesson Keeps Me Buying
items.summary: Three companies control the world's DRAM supply, AI is burning through memory faster than fabs can build it, and one of those three just signed contracts that could permanently rewire what a chip cycle looks like.

items.title: TSMC Price Prediction: One Number Could Define the Stock’s Next Move
items.summary: TSMC is up over 66% in the past year, AI customers are booking capacity years out, and the only foundry rival is hemorrhaging billions. So why does one critical number still cast doubt on how high this stock can actually go?

items.title: Prediction: This AI Stock Could Be the Next One to Shock Wall Street
items.summary: Micron has already stunned Wall Street with a historic surge, but a fresh competitive threat just knocked shares down and reignited the debate over whether the AI memory trade still has legs or has finally run out of road.

items.title: Intel Climbs 3% on Chip Price Hike Report a Day After Piper Sandler Went Neutral; AMD Rises 2%, Taiwan Semiconductor Drifts
items.summary: A report of Intel raising chip prices sent shares surging 3% and erased the prior session's Piper Sandler-driven selloff, but the real question is whether the company has genuine pricing power or is simply charging scarcity rent that evaporates the moment supply loosens.

items.title: How Far Could Intel Stock Fall After More Than Quadrupling In A Year?
items.summary: Intel (INTC) stock fell 5.6% on September 10 and trades near $100, about 29% below its 52-week high. Even so, it has returned 310.5% over the past year. The question is how much of that a market shock could take back, and on average Intel has fallen harder than the S&P 500 when shocks hit.
